workflow: Multiple threads advance the same shared iterator toward exhaustion concurrently.
Each thread observes the iterator’s still-present owner reference and enters the exhaustion cleanup path.
Because clearing and releasing the owner reference are not coordinated, more than one thread releases the same reference, corrupting the referenced object’s ownership count.
A thread still performing the iteration uses a borrowed pointer after another thread’s release has freed the referenced object.
The stale access or later ownership validation terminates the process instead of completing iteration safely.
summary: Concurrent iterator exhaustion double-releases shared state and invalidates an in-flight traversal
decision_reason: No existing cluster is materially identical: the failure combines a race in one-time ownership release with an in-flight borrowed traversal of the released object. Existing double-free and concurrent-reference clusters involve different cleanup or mutation workflows.
